questions.question: How do you release a converter dolly's air brakes before coupling?

options.text: Remove the dolly parking brake control.

questions.explanation: If a converter dolly has air brakes, open the air tank petcock to release them. You must release the brakes before positioning the dolly in front of the rear trailer.

questions.question: When driving, what is important to do?

options.text: Plan how to handle dangerous situations.
Turn your head all the way around instead of using mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to handle dangerous situations.
questions.explanation: Watch the road constantly for hazards. Think about what you will do if these hazards become emergencies.

questions.question: When should you watch for black ice?

options.text: When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
When the temperature is above freezing and there is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
questions.explanation: Black ice is thin, clear ice. You can see the road through it. Watch for it when the temperature is below freezing and the road surface looks wet.

questions.question: When uncoupling, where should the landing gear be?
questions.explanation: When uncoupling, lower the landing gear to touch the ground firmly. If the trailer is loaded, turn the crank a few more times to remove some weight from the trailer.

questions.question: What happens to a vehicle's speed when going downhill?
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls a vehicle downhill and makes its speed increase.

questions.question: When driving a trailer with ABS, how should you brake?

options.text: Use less brake pressure than you would without ABS.
Use extra braking force to make ABS activate.
Brake the same way you would without ABS.
Brake less often than you would without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would without ABS.
questions.explanation: When driving a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: What causes brake fade?
questions.explanation: Overusing brakes causes them to overheat and work less effectively. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: How do you release a converter dolly's spring brakes before coupling?

options.text: Use the dolly parking brake control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the dolly parking brake control.
questions.explanation: If a converter dolly has spring brakes, use the parking brake control to release them. You must release the brakes before positioning the dolly in front of the rear trailer.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, what is your best option to stop?

options.text: Hit a slower vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Use an escape ramp if your brakes fail going downhill. If no ramp is available, look for another escape route such as a side road or open field.

questions.question: When starting from a stop, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle should shift to the right.
The vehicle should be put into third gear.
The vehicle should not roll backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle should not roll backward.
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when starting from a complete stop. This prevents hitting anything behind you.

questions.question: When checking your windshield wiper blades, they should be:
questions.explanation: Check your wiper blades for damage and cracks. They should be firmly attached to your windshield.

questions.question: One way to handle blind spots is to:

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles so they cannot pass you.
Drive in the left lane so you only watch vehicles on your right.
Check your mirrors often and know where nearby vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often and know where nearby vehicles are.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently to watch traffic around you. This helps you see vehicles that may be in your blind spots.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a type of retarder?
questions.explanation: Retarders are devices that help slow a vehicle without using the brakes. The four types are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.

questions.question: When uncoupling, you should move the dolly out from under the rear trailer ____ unlocking the pintle hook.
questions.explanation: Never unlock the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the rear trailer. The tow bar could flip up and cause serious injury.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when used:
questions.explanation: If the brakes pull to one side, there is a problem with your brakes. Have them inspected.

questions.question: Without oil in its engine, a vehicle:

options.text: Will make quick jerks while driving.
May have its engine damaged quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have its engine damaged quickly.
questions.explanation: An engine can be destroyed quickly without oil. Do not drive if your oil pressure gauge is low or moving.

questions.question: When traveling down a hill:

options.text: You will slow to a stop.

questions.explanation: Gravity pulls your vehicle down a slope and makes it go faster.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the air tanks falls below 60 psi?

options.text: A warning light will come on.
The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning light will come on.
questions.explanation: When air pressure drops below 60 psi, a warning light or wig wag signal should turn on.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Pull out the air brake knob.

questions.explanation: To make a normal stop with air brakes, press the brake pedal down.

questions.question: When approaching a construction worker near the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Always slow down in work zones. Reduce your speed when workers are on or near the road.
